decisions.executionNote: Approach wrench and pliers in separate workspaces, gradually pitching open grippers downward; table height and tool offsets are initially uncertain.
Retry approach with half-sized increments after zero-step continuity rejection.
Complete top-down orientation while moving above wrench handle and plier handles, retaining elbow-up continuity and clearance.
Reduce rejected approach increments to preserve continuous IK; continue above the two tools.
Replan from measured pose after interruption. Raise slightly while completing downward pitch and correcting inward tool alignment; surface appears higher than initial estimate.
Lower open downward-facing grippers toward the wrench handle and plier handles, using small depth increments before closing.
At apparent tabletop contact, close around the two handles and make a short test lift; verify actual retention in images.
Both tools appear retained on the test lift. Carry inward above the toolbox while preserving clearance, then inspect matching recess geometry.
Wrench has visibly slipped onto the hammer; left hand is empty. Hold the retained pliers aside and inspect the toolbox recesses from above before placement.
Lower away from the guarded posture. Return left toward the slipped wrench while rotating retained pliers toward the upper horizontal recess; matching orientation remains uncertain.
Right IK approached a folded limit; descend and slightly retreat before further inward transport. Left approaches the wrench with yaw aligned to its diagonal handle.
Align left grasp farther along exposed wrench handle. Move retained pliers slowly over the upper tray recess while maintaining lower, continuous elbow-up posture.
Regrasp exposed wrench. Retreat right wrist and tilt toward the tray to gain fingertip reach without entering the rejected folded posture; keep pliers closed.
Lift left vertically to check wrench retention. Right wrist view no longer confirms pliers in hand, so open and move aside to reacquire rather than assume a grasp.
Wrench now stays between left fingers on vertical lift. Carry it gently toward the left tray recess, undoing diagonal yaw. Right approaches the visibly displaced pliers for a fresh grasp.
Lower retained wrench over the left longitudinal recess. Reorient right gripper across the displaced plier handle and correct forward/left alignment.
Wrench has yawed against the tray rim; lift clear and align its observed head toward the back. Correct right gripper orientation to the pliers' actual length before closing.
Neither tool is securely centered in the fingers now. Withdraw open left hand for a fresh grasp and move right to the isolated tape measure, away from the crowded tray rim.
Center right open gripper over the tape measure. Align left closing direction across the wrench now lying diagonally at the tray edge.
Make a small centering correction, close and test-lift the tape. Move empty left hand toward the exposed hammer rather than pinch the tray rim.
Tape remains between right fingers; transport inward slowly with extra clearance. Align left gripper with the hammer handle and descend for a clean grasp.
Close on centered hammer handle and test-lift. Carry the tape toward the small upper-right recess, keeping wrist height below the earlier folded IK limit.
Raise both retained tools to clear the tray rim. Bring hammer inward while straightening its length, and tilt the right wrist forward for tape-slot reach with less elbow folding.
Images show both tools slipped, not placed. Reapproach the nearby hammer and tape with open grippers at a deeper grip height; next transport will avoid rotation.
Settle and close the left grasp before lifting. Tape has tipped beside the rim; raise slightly and correct right alignment using the wrist image.
Lift hammer vertically without yaw. Right shows contact-induced tracking error beside the tray, so withdraw upward/outward before retrying tape alignment.
Carry hammer above the rim without changing its orientation. Rotate empty right gripper so its fingers run beside, rather than into, the tray wall when grasping the tape.
Guide hammer farther over the central longitudinal recess, compensating its visible yaw gently. Descend right beside the wall with fingers oriented clear of the rim.
Hammer has slipped against the rim again; withdraw empty left hand. Correct right grasp toward the tape in the rotated wrist view, then close and inspect.
Tape is now centered between right fingers. Lift vertically well clear of the toolbox rim before any lateral placement motion; leave left stationary.
Test lift showed tape remained on the table. Reopen and descend farther around its sides, with a small centering correction; no success assumed.
Use the wrist image to center tape between the finger pads and lower another centimeter before closing; keep the other arm still.
Tape is now enclosed deeper between the pads. Lift vertically with unchanged orientation and inspect retention before carrying.
Tape visibly retained. Carry slowly over the right square recess with added rim clearance; small forward tilt and wrist retreat preserve elbow-up reach.
Lower retained tape slowly into the small right-hand square recess, correcting slightly inward and forward. Inspect seating before opening.
Tape has contacted the recess area. Open to let it settle, then withdraw slightly upward/back for an unobstructed seating check.
Tape is released inside the tray but appears perched at the recess edge. Gently guide it forward toward the square seat while withdrawing left for visibility.
Tape is standing on an edge. Shift the closed fingertips inward over its upper face and gently guide it down rather than pushing its lower edge forward.
Leave released tape in its recess region for now and clear the right hand. Reapproach the hammer at a more central handle point with its current diagonal orientation.
Center and close left gripper around the hammer handle. Approach the displaced pliers with forward tilt, preserving wrist reach and staying on the right side.
Left contact is on slippery chrome; reopen and shift onto the rubber handle. Lower right toward the plier neck/handles with the observed forward tilt.
Stop descending at rim contact. Close at the measured poses around the exposed handles, let closure settle, and test retention with a small vertical lift.
Hammer handle is visibly offset from the closed left pads; recenter and close again. Continue the right vertical lift to establish whether the plier-neck grasp retains it.
Test the left grasp with a straight lift clear of the rim. Right missed the plier head; reopen and shift toward its wider handles at a lower depth.
Hammer appears retained; raise and retreat slightly while moving inward to clear the snagging rim before alignment. Close right pads at the visible plier neck, then make a small test lift.
The plier grasp is too shallow with the strongly tilted wrist. Reopen, pitch nearer vertical and advance at lower wrist height to put the pads around the tool rather than above it.

After the rejected forward suffix, close right at the observed neck alignment, then retreat slightly during a test lift. Reapproach the hammer handle outside the front rim, where a deeper grasp is unobstructed.
Refine both visible offsets and grasp deeper: hammer below the front rim, pliers around the yellow neck rather than the metal tip. Settle closed before lifting.
Lift left clear of the front rim to test retention. Right is obstructed near the tape/box; withdraw outward and upward from the measured pose rather than forcing the failed descent.
Raise retained hammer and align its length while clear of the rim. Retry pliers at the exposed metal head, away from the tape obstruction, with a more vertical approach.
Replan from the interrupted poses: lower right without further forward motion to reduce folding and approach the exposed plier head. Finish gentle hammer yaw alignment while retaining clearance.
Carry hammer above the central tray with no further rotation. Center the exposed plier head between right pads using the wrist image, then close at the measured low approach height.
Advance no farther into the rejected right posture; use a small fingertip tilt, close, then retreat during test lift. Lower retained hammer slowly into the central-left recess region.

Straighten the hammer's observed diagonal alignment above the longitudinal recess while lowering slightly. For pliers, correct the remaining pad offset with fingertip tilt rather than more guarded forward wrist motion.
Hammer is no longer retained and appears supported in the tray; open and clear left for inspection. Right pads still appear shallow on the plier head, so descend another small amount before closing.
Test-lift the deeper plier-head grasp with slight wrist retreat. Approach the isolated wrench handle using left hand while the hammer rests in the tray.
Align left pads perpendicular to the wrench handle. Plier test lift again failed; withdraw open right hand and change closing direction to grasp the wider pivot clear of the tape obstruction.
Close and test-lift the centered wrench handle. Lower the newly oriented right gripper over the plier pivot, using small forward increments with simultaneous descent.
Wrench is retained on the first lift; raise further before crossing the tray rim. Move right pads slightly farther over the plier pivot and close after the low approach.
Wrench has tilted downward while held; raise enough for its head to clear the rim before insertion. Test-lift the newly enclosed plier pivot with rearward wrist motion to avoid folding.

Both tools slipped on lifting. Reapproach wrench lower on its handle. Change right grasp to the black plier handle, with closing direction across it and forward tilt to avoid the crowded metal-head approach.
Lower left pads around the wrench handle. Correct right toward the black plier handle using the rotated wrist view, staying clear of the tape and reducing wrist height gradually.
At the measured contact poses, close around the wrench handle and one exposed black plier handle. Settle closure, then perform a very small vertical retention test.
Move the wrench grasp toward its heavier neck to reduce repeated pitch slipping. Withdraw the empty right hand from the crowded tape/plier edge and focus on a stable left placement.
The tray blocks the crosswise neck approach. Raise slightly and orient left fingers parallel to the wall over the wrench's heavy head; keep right clear.
Lower around the wrench head with fingers clear of the wall, then close and settle before testing retention.
